# OpenEXR controls

These inert controls are generated by the independent OpenEXR 3.3.3 / Imath
3.1.12 library using the retained C++ encoder, then mutated by independent
Python field writers under `docs/edr/native-engine/audits/2026-11-07-v249-exr`.
The Go decoder does not generate its own expected outputs.

`manifest.json` pins 291 EXR inputs and their ClamAV 1.5.4 sigtool hashes or
reference rejection. There are 218 accepted and 73 rejected controls. Where
available, a separate C++ decoder supplies exact RGB8 bytes in `.rgb` files;
accepted cases without that oracle retain native hash/rule comparisons.
Native and independent library identities are in the audit's reference
manifest. Ordinary Go tests require neither library nor executable.

The controls cover raw, RLE, ZIP1/ZIP16, PIZ, PXR24, B44/B44A, mixed HALF/
FLOAT/UINT channels, linear B44 channels, flat/NaN/extreme values, scanlines,
tiles, mip/rip maps with both rounding modes, and multipart RGB selection.
The wide PIZ input forces the wide wavelet path. Separate raw-block controls
exercise DWA/HTJ2K tags whose compressed algorithms the reference cannot
execute. Deep-data and subsampling controls are rejected by that reference.

Metadata/chunk controls cover crop/padding and reversed windows, data origins,
advisory version bits, required and optional fields, name lengths, duplicate
channels, block coordinate quantization, aliased offsets, unexpected levels,
physical truncation, checksums/trailers, and advisory PIZ/Huffman lengths.
Late controls distinguish an omitted part type from an explicit empty type,
validate typed byte arrays and nonnegative maximum-sample metadata, and
exercise large unknown type rejection without copying its full value.

`half_rgb8.bin` separately enumerates all 65,536 binary16 patterns using
Python's standard binary16 decoder and independent clamp/round arithmetic.
SHA-256: `e4941ba773dfb43adc14ae4f58275e276a23f860c8dbaa2ec23d0989d884af7c`.
It is not an EXR fixture and is outside the EXR-row manifest.

Native positive rules use explicit harmless image file-type overlays.
Builtin-only default classifier probes retain EXR as binary data. These
controls establish decoding and controlled signature paths, not malware
recall, fleet false-positive rates or exhaustive cross-platform parity.
